All levels (Bachelor, Master’s, and PhD) of inbound exchange students are eligible. 
Lecturers in Engineering, Business or Architecture related areas are welcome for teaching mobility at HCMUT. 
Non-academic staff (esp. from International Office) from partner universaities are welcome for one week mobility. 
One credit is equivalent to 50 hours of standardized learning time for the learner, including the time for scheduled 
lectures, guided instruction, self-study, research, experiential learning, and assessments/exams. 
For classroom teaching activities, one credit requires a minimum of 15 hours of lectures or 30 hours of practical 
work, experiments, discussions, in which one classroom hour is counted as 50 minutes. 
The teaching activities are organized between 06:00 and before 22:00 (periods 1 to 16) on all days of the week from 
Monday to Sunday. The scheduling of other learning activities related to the training program will be based on specific 
situations or particular academic levels. 
Classes are generally conducted face-to-face. 
Online learning is oraganized depending on specific situations in accordance with the academic regulations. 
All lecturers are required to use “Bach Khoa e-learning – BkeL” (an internal online platform at HCMUT) to facilitate 
their teaching activities and share course-related materials/documents to students.

In that case, we can refer students to student housing agents. 
Our Office for International Study Programs can support international students in 
registering for the dormitory.  
Contact: oisp@hcmut.edu.vn

VI. Other 
 
Accommodation: 100 – 300 USD 
Food: 200 -300 USD 
Transportation (bus): 10 – 150 USD (depending in the students’ choice of transportation) 
Utilities: 5 -15 USD 
Personal expense: 35 – 85 USD 
Total: 350 – 850 USD 
Students who stay at HCMUT for academic exchange period are required to obtain a study visa before entering 
Vietnam, following the procedures below. 
1. After finalizing and signing a Learning Agreement, HCMUT sends students a visa request form to fill in. 
2. HCMUT submits all documents of the students’ study period to the Vietnamese Immigration Department 
for issuing the Visa Approval Letter. 
3. HCMUT sends the scanned Visa Approval Letter + Acceptance Letter to the students. 
4. The incoming students bring their original passports and the provided Visa Letter to the expected Vietnamese 
Embassy/Consulate in their home country to collect the visa. 
Notes:  
- The Visa Approval Letter issued by the Immigration Department will enable the students to obtain a visa shortly. 
- The incoming students had better NOT apply for a tourist visa before receiving the Visa Approval Letter. A tourist visa 
doesn’t mean for study purposes and will not be accepted for an exchange stay at HCMUT.  
 
 
 
The students need to submit a Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) application to our university with other required 
documents. We will submit the completed CoE application to the immigration office in Kyoto. As soon as we 
receive the CoE from the immigration office, we will send it to the student or the international office of your 
university by post. When the students receive the CoE, please have them apply immediately for a visa at the 
nearest Japanese embassy/consulate in your country. 
Before students leave their countries, we strongly recommend that they obtain travel insurance, which covers 
difficulties, medical helps or incidents during travel from and back to their countries. 
The students are required to provide a copy of their insurance to HCMUT one week before their arrival. 
Imcoming students from HCMUT’s partners with valid agreements can benefit from tuition waivers. 
Exchange students can have the opportunity to receive scholarship s to partly cover necessary expenses 
during their mobility period. 
We may decline to accept students according to our capacity, the changes in the circumstances due to infectious 
disease prevalence or natural disasters. 
Regarding COVID-19, students must follow the Vietnamese government / HCMUTguidelines. Please note that HCMUT 
may refuse to accept students if future immigration restrictions are imposed by the Vietnamese government.

CHITKARAU – AN EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCE OF MIND & SPIRIT.
COME, EXPLORE YOUR POTENTIAL 
 
We are nestled at the foothills of the mighty Himalayas in the most planned, secure, and
beautiful city of Chandigarh, designed by French Architect Le Corbusier, with two spectacular
campuses. The city boasts of a dense green cover, easy accessibility by air, road, and rail, and
sumptuous Indian and Western cuisines from all parts of India and the world. Yoga, mindfulness,
and meditation are practiced at the campus with unforgettable trips in the Himalayas, and so
much more. This brochure is a window to all the opportunities India and Chitkara University will
throw up for you. Come explore us, and your Potential

The Golden Temple in Amritsar, officially Harmandir Sahib, is Sikhism’s holiest shrine and a
masterpiece of sacred architecture. Nestled within a shimmering man-made pool called the Amrit
Sarovar, its gilded façade and marble inlays reflect the devotion of generations. Pilgrims and visitors of
all faiths come to offer prayers, listen to continuous recitation of the Guru Granth Sahib, and partake
in the langar, a free community meal served to thousands daily. The temple’s peaceful atmosphere,
historic significance, and commitment to equality and service make it a symbol of spiritual solace and
communal harmony in India, welcoming seekers from everywhere.

TANTALIZE YOUR TASTE
BUDS 
INDIAN CUISINE 
Cook, taste, and learn
diverse Indian cuisines in
our culinary sessions!

REJUVENATE
YOUR
BODY MIND
and soul
Join our refreshing campus
yoga sessions for balance and
energy!

WE ARE AT THE FOREFRONT OF INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENT & PARTNERSHIPS
 
Name any part of the World, and we send and receive students. From North America to Europe,
the Middle East to Southeast Asia, from Japan & Korea to down under Australia, our students go
everywhere, and we welcome their students to Chitkara University. Chandigarh is the most well-
planned, secure, and non-polluted Indian city in the foothills of the Himalayas, where our
international students and faculty love to keep coming back. 
Chitkara University offers a diverse range of programs in Engineering, Business, Pharmacy, Health
Sciences, Design, Media, Hospitality, Education, Law, and more. With a student-centric approach,
the university ensures holistic development by combining academic rigor with practical exposure,
entrepreneurship, and skill enhancement. 
 
Our experiential learning is not just limited to academic education but a holistic one that engages
and rejuvenates your mind and body alike. From Yoga to Meditation, trekking and soul searching
trips in the upper reaches of the Himalayas, students experience a vibe and energy of India that it
has represented for centuries. Besides, you will be welcomed to learn and indulge in vibrant and
lip-smacking Indian cuisines from diverse parts of India, and create some lifelong relationships with
our community that could be a bedrock support for life. 
 
You can come to us for a short mobility or a semester or global internships, we abide by our motto
‘Athithi Devo Bhava’, which simply translates to our guests are our Gods. Come, experience our
Hospitality and grow in your mind and spirit at Chitkara University

His Holiness 14th Dalai Lama at the
Global Week 2019

Student Exchange Program
FACT SHEET
2027 Spring

■ General Information of the Institution
■ Office of International Affairs
■ Nomination and Application Deadline
Name  Seoul National University of Science and Technology (SeoulTech)
Website  www.seoultech.ac.kr
Mailing
Address
 #115, International Hall building (No.38), SeoulTech, 232 Gongneung-ro, Nowon-gu, 
  Seoul, Republic of Korea (postal code: 01811)
Website  https://irt.seoultech.ac.kr/
Tel  (Incoming) +82-2-970-9216 / (Outgoing) +82-2-970-9214 / (Short-term Program) +82-2-970-9215
Email  exchange_seoultech@seoultech.ac.kr
Spring semester Fall semester
Nomination Deadline October 15 April 15
Application Deadline October 31 April 30
1. General Information
2. Nomination / Application Information

■ Application Documents (in English)
 - 1st Application Document Submission: 
  
  - 2nd Application Document Submission: 
  - Only for Dormitory Applicants: 
No. Document For OECD Nationality For non-OECD Nationality Notes
1 Online Application ● ●  Application link will be sent to student who have been officially 
 nominated by student home university
2 Certificate of Enrollment ● ●
 (For non-OECD Nationality): Original required to SeoulTech
 - For Apostille member countries: Notarized with an Apostille
 - For non-Apostille countries: Authenticated by the Korean Embassy/Consulate
   ※ CHN students: CHSI only
3 Official Transcript ● ●
 (For non-OECD Nationality): Original required to SeoulTech
 - For Apostille member countries: Notarized with an Apostille
 - For non-Apostille countries: Authenticated by the Korean Embassy/Consulate
4 Certificate of 
Language Proficiency ● ●
5 Study Plan ● ●  [Form 1] attached
6 Copy of Valid Passport ● ●  Valid for at least 6 months from the semester start date
7 Photo ● ●  Passport-sized: 3.5cm×4.5cm
No. Document For OECD Nationality For non-OECD Nationality Notes
1 Copy of Korea Visa ● ●
2 Flight Itinerary ● ●
3 Bank Statement ● ●
 Bank statement under the applicant’s own name 
 - One semester: USD 6,000 / Two semesters: USD 12,000
 (For non-OECD Nationality): Original required to SeoulTech
No. Document Notes
1 TB test result  - Negative Tuberculosis(TB) test result
 - Available tests: Chest X-ray, blood test OR skin test
2 M easles Vaccination Certificate  - Proof of 2 doses

■ Language requirement
 Applicants are required to have a good command of either English (B2 level) OR Korean (TOPIK Level 3) 
in order to communicate and function effectively in an academic environment. Therefore, an 
internationally recognized language certificate equivalent to these levels is required.
 ▶ TOEIC 750 / IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL 72 / Cambridge English Scale 160 / Global Scale of English 
(Pearson) 59 / DET 100
    OR
 ▶ TOPIK(Test of Proficiency in Korean) Level 3
    ※ Students who apply to the exchange program using a TOPIK score will be permitted to 
enroll in Korean-language-taught courses only.
■ Number of exchanges students
 Due to accommodation capacity and course registration constraints, SeoulTech has implemented 
a strategic enrollment limitation starting from the 2024 academic year. This decision reflects our 
commitment to maintaining high standards of education, fostering a conducive learning 
environment, and ensuring that each student receives personalized attention and support.
 We will strive to maintain a balanced number of inbound and outbound exchange students.
 If none of SeoulTech students have participated in your exchange program during the past two 
semesters only one open seat will be allocated to your university. 
 Please note that we are unable to accept more than two students from each partner university 
per semester. If there is any uncertainty regarding the quota, we strongly recommend contacting 
SeoulTech in advance before beginning your selection process.
■ Academic Calendar
■ Courses
 - Course List (https://global.seoultech.ac.kr/bound/inbound/course)
   The finalized list of courses offered in English for each semester will be announced 
approximately one month before the start of the semester. In the meantime, please refer to 
the course list from the previous semester. Please note that exchange students are allowed to 
select courses only from the Module list.
 - Syllabus
   For students’ convenience, we have gathered all the syllabi for the Module courses on Google Drive.
   ▶ (2026 Spring Semester)
       https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1IGgr8Y7103xdRg0X1qAMuHqznIbMtXmJ?usp=sharing
   ▶ (2026 Fall Semester)
       https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1wzP4AnJfZKSYiJqh7XX_MxEePq3Pf0rf?usp=sharing
  ※ Please note that course offerings are relatively flexible and may be added or removed for the upcom ing 
semester. Therefore, students whose home universities have strict academic requirements, such as specific 
mandatory courses, should be aware that our university cannot guarantee the availability of particular courses.
3. Academic Information
 2027 Spring Semester  March 2, 2027 ~ June 21, 2027

■ Intensive Korean Language Course Program  (https://klc.seoultech.ac.kr/en/course/registration/)
 Exchange students may enroll in an intensive Korean Language Course Program. This is a 
non-credit course, and students are required to pay the tuition fee.
■ Grading System
 All exchange students can take (Min) 2 credits ~ (Max) 18 credits per semester.
 1 Credit = 16 teaching hours including lectures, exam, assignments, and attendance
 1 Course = 2 or 3 credits
 All courses are offered on a semester basis and run for 16 weeks.
■ Assessment
※ The lowest passing grade is D0(60.)
※ Assessment can be subject to change

■ National Health Insurance Service (NHIS)
 National Health Insurance is a mandatory program implemented by the Ministry of Health and 
Welfare in Korea and is not optional. It applies regardless of whether students have private 
insurance. Once students apply for their Alien Registration Card (ARC) after arrival in Korea and 
the physical card is issued, their information will be updated in the National Health Insurance 
system, and they will be automatically enrolled.
 As of 2026, the monthly National Health Insurance premium is KRW 79,310. Payment notices are 
sent each month to the student’s registered residence in Korea.
■ Korean buddy program & International Student Club (ISC)
 ISC (International Student Club) is a student organization at SeoulTech that operates a buddy 
program for international students. During their stay in Korea, exchange students are supported

How to get to Zlín
Zlín, a vibrant Moravian city in the Czech Republic, is well-connected by various transportation options. Whether you want to get here by plane, train, bus, or car, here is how you can reach Zlín efficiently:
By plane
Unfortunately, Zlín does not have its international airport. The Václav Havel Airport Prague (PRG) is the air gate to the Czech Republic with daily connections from/to major European cities. More information about flight timetables and transport connections from/to the airport are available on the website of
Václav Havel Airport Prague
. There are reliable and frequent connections from Prague airport to the city center by
public transport
and
special airport buses
(AE – Airport Express). There is the possibility of buying tickets, including from/to airport transport and tickets for connecting buses/trains to Zlín.
Other options frequently used by our international students are to fly to Bratislava (Slovakia) – approx. 150km from Zlín, Vienna (Austria) – approx. 180km from Zlín, Katowice (Poland) – approx. 215km from Zlín, or Kraków (Poland) – approx. 290km from Zlín. There are train or bus connections to Zlín from all of these cities.
By train
The Czech Republic has an extensive railway network, operated by four major railway companies:
České dráhy
(ČD, Czech Railways),
RegioJet
,
LEO Express
,
and
Arriva
. The timetables and connections are changing approximately once per year. Due to that, we recommend checking the connections at the websites of the mentioned railway companies.
Zlín itself has several train stations even though they are all quite small. The main train station is called
Zlín – Střed
and it has only one direct train from Prague (
Zlínský expres
). However, the neighbouring town
Otrokovice
is placed on the main train corridor. Due to that, it is possible to get directly from Otrokovice to five European capitals (Bratislava, Budapest, Prague, Vienna, and Warsaw). So, it is possible to search for the connections to Otrokovice and then use the public transportation working between Zlín and Otrokovice.
Traveling by České dráhy
Tickets are sold at most of the train stations, and it is not mandatory to purchase your tickets online. However, we recommend buying them online because the online reservation goes together with the free seat reservation inside the train. Then you can download the ticket to your mobile device without the necessity of printing it for the domestic trains. The international trains might require a ticket to be printed due to the incompatibility of national systems. The company provides first- and second-class travel. Most of the scheduled trains stop at Otrokovice, where it is possible to change for a local train going in the direction of Zlín Střed, or it is possible to use the public transportation mentioned above.
Traveling by RegioJet
RegioJet provides service on the arterial train lines. In combination with their buses, it is possible to get to Zlín from major Czech cities. If you travel with RegioJet, we highly recommend you buy your tickets online. From Prague, it is possible to take their yellow train from the main Prague train station to Olomouc, where a connecting RegioJet bus to Zlín is available.
Traveling by LEO Express
LEO Express trains go from Prague main train station to Přerov, where you can change to a bus or a train to Zlín. The company no longer operates trains, or buses to Zlín, or Otrokovice.
Traveling by Arriva
At this moment, there are no train connections provided by Arriva on the track between Prague and Zlín. Nevertheless, Arriva operates several regional train tracks in the Zlín region.
By bus
If you do not like traveling by train, you can use a large network of coach lines instead. Usually, buses are more frequent, and slightly cheaper than trains. The Czech Republic has connections from/to major European cities several times a week. Most international buses arrive in Prague (Florenc AN) or Brno (Zvonařka AN). Several buses get you to Zlín from Prague and Brno each day. Further information on train and bus connections within the Czech Republic is available at
idos.cz
.
By car
Zlín is connected to the Czech motorway network thanks to highways D49 and D55. You can easily get to the country’s major cities (Brno, Olomouc, Ostrava, and Prague) from here. In the Czech Republic, it is mandatory to have an e-vignette for using a
motorway
. There are four available versions of the e-vignettes:
1 day for
CZK 210
(EUR 8.40; USD 8.95)
10 days for
CZK 290
(EUR 11.60; USD 12.35)
1 month for
CZK 460
(EUR 18.35; USD 19.60)
1 year for

Welcome to the Faculty of Education UWB
As an Erasmus student coming to study in Pilsen at the Faculty of Education, you can choose any course from the sections mentioned below. Check with your university how many credits you need to bring back and choose courses according to your preferences. Keep in mind that your courses should be linked to what you study at your home university. It is up to your university which courses they recognize.
Feel free to combine courses from all the sections (see below).
If you have any questions, contact us. We are here for you.

FAQ
Here you will find answers to the most common questions about studying and living in Plzeň. Our FAQ is designed to help you prepare for your stay and make your arrival smoother.
Are there any required travel documents?
Do I need international insurance?
How do I get a passport or visa? Do I need a visa?
How can I budget for my study abroad?
Where can I buy inexpensive flights?

Are there any required travel documents?
Yes, you will need a valid passport to enter the Czech Republic. Depending on your nationality, you may also need a visa or residence permit. Make sure your passport is valid for the entire duration of your stay.
Back
Do I need international insurance?
Yes. All incoming students are required to have valid health insurance that covers medical care in the Czech Republic. EU/EEA students can use their European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). Non-EU students must arrange private health insurance approved for use in the Czech Republic.
Back
How do I get a passport or visa? Do I need a visa?
If you are from the EU/EEA or Switzerland, you do not need a visa to study in the Czech Republic. Students from other countries will need to apply for a long-term visa or residence permit. Please contact the Czech Embassy or Consulate in your home country for details.
Back
How can I budget for my study abroad?
The cost of living in the Czech Republic is relatively affordable compared to many European countries. On average, students should budget around 400–700 EUR per month for accommodation, food, transportation, and personal expenses. Keep in mind that travel, study materials, and leisure activities may add extra costs.
Back
Where can I buy inexpensive flights?
Popular platforms such as Skyscanner, Kiwi, or Google Flights can help you compare prices. For flights within Europe, low-cost airlines (e.g., Ryanair, Wizz Air, EasyJet) often offer budget-friendly options. Booking in advance usually ensures better prices.
Back
Where can I find lodging abroad?
Our university provides student dormitories, which are the most affordable and convenient option. If you prefer private housing, you can explore rental websites, student Facebook groups, or real estate agencies in Plzeň. We recommend arranging accommodation before your arrival.
Back
What should I pack?
Pack according to the length of your stay and the seasons. Winters in the Czech Republic can be cold (down to -10 °C), so bring warm clothing, while summers can be hot. Don’t forget essentials such as travel documents, insurance papers, medications, study materials, and adaptors for European sockets (Type C/E).
Back
How do I stay safe while traveling abroad?
The Czech Republic is considered a safe country. Still, follow general safety rules: keep your documents in a secure place, be cautious in crowded areas, and know the local emergency number (112). It is also a good idea to register with your embassy and stay informed about local laws and customs.
Back
How do I get from the airport to Plzeň?
Most international students arrive via Prague Airport (Václav Havel Airport). From there, you can take a direct bus or use public transport to reach the main train or bus station in Prague. Regular trains and buses connect Prague to Plzeň, and the journey takes about 1–1.5 hours. Tickets cost around 5–10 EUR.
Back
What student support services are available?
The International Office and the Study Department are here to help you with academic and administrative issues. The university also offers counseling services, a Career Centre, a library, and IT support. Through the Buddy Program, local students can help you settle in and navigate your new environment.
Back
What are the language requirements? Do I need to speak Czech?
Courses for international students are offered in English, so Czech is not required for studying. However, learning some basic Czech phrases can be very useful for everyday life, such as shopping or traveling. Some faculties even offer free or low-cost Czech language courses for international students.
Back
Can I work while studying in the Czech Republic?
EU/EEA and Swiss students can work without restrictions. Non-EU students are allowed to work part-time during their studies, but depending on the type of visa, some restrictions may apply. It is recommended to check the exact conditions with the Czech Ministry of Interior.
Back
What public transportation is available in Plzeň?
Plzeň has an excellent public transport system including trams, buses, and trolleybuses. Students can buy discounted monthly passes (around 12–15 EUR) for unlimited travel. Tickets are available at kiosks, online, or via mobile apps.
Back
What is your question?
Plzeň is a vibrant university city with a rich cultural scene. Students can join various clubs, sports activities, and student organizations. There are concerts, festivals, and plenty of opportunities to explore Czech traditions as well as international communities. You can take a look on
https://www.visitplzen.eu/en/
Back
Where can I find information about courses and registration?
All course information is available in the university’s online system (STAG). The Study Department and your faculty coordinators will guide you through course registration and requirements before the semester begins.
Back
What is the cost of student dormitories and meals?
Dormitory accommodation usually costs 100–130 EUR per month, depending on the type of room. Student canteens (menza) offer affordable meals starting from 2–4 EUR. Many students combine dormitory living with cooking or eating out in local restaurants, which are also reasonably priced
Back
Whom can I contact in case of emergency?
In the Czech Republic, the general emergency number is
112
. You can also directly call the police (158), ambulance (155), or fire service (150). At the university, the International Office and your student buddy can help you in urgent situations.
Back

Academic Credit System
SeoulTech offers the following Inbound Programs:
▶ Student Exchange Program
:
Students can enroll in up to six academic credit courses.
* The Student Exchange Program at SeoulTech allows students from
partner universities
to pursue their studies for one or two semesters at SeoulTech.
* Students who are officially nominated by their home universities will have the opportunity to apply for the Student Exchange Program at SeoulTech.
* Tuition will be waived under the student exchange agreement.
▶
Visiting(Fee-paying) Program
:
Students can enroll in up to six academic credit courses.
* Open to students enrolled at
both partner and non-partner universities
of SeoulTech.
* Participants will have the chance to take credit courses to pursue their studies for one or two semesters at SeoulTech.
* Students must be officially nominated by their home universities.
* Although students in the Visiting Program are granted the same status as exchange students, they are not eligible for tuition waivers.
■
Eligibility
Exchange student who wishes to study at SeoulTech must;
- Completed at least (Undergraduate) two semesters / (Graduate) one semester at student’s home university
- Be enrolled as a full-time student at home university that has an active student exchange agreement with SeoulTech
- Be nominated as an exchange student candidate by student home university
- Be able to study in either English or Korean for at least one semester (4.5 months)
- Have not studied at any other Korean university in the previous semester
■

Application Documents
- Online application: Application link will be sent to student who have been officially nominated by student home university
- Certificate of Enrollment (※ original required to SeoulTech)
- Official Transcript
(※ original required to SeoulTech)
- Certificate of Language Proficiency (English or Korean)
- Study Plan
- Copy of Valid Passport
- Photo (Passport-sized: 3.5cm×4.5cm)

Reader's Guide
Welcome to Xiamen University Libraries. This Guide will help you navigate the library to find books and articles, study spaces, facilities, and different ways of getting in touch with librarians. We hope that you will find the guide useful in your library research and that you have an enjoyable experience using the Libraries.
Libraries
The Library consists of seven libraries, including Main Library, Dewang Library, Tan KahKee College Library, Economics & Business Library, Information & Engineering Library, Law Library, and Art Library.
Library Cards
Xiamen University registered students, faculty, instructors, lecturers and staffs use campus card as library card for borrowing materials and for access to libraries and other areas requiring a library card. All library privileges are required to have library card activated first.
For inter-university exchange program students, library card will be activated automatically within one week after registration in XMU International Students'''' Affairs Division.
For college-invited exchange students, a borrowing application form completely filled out, signed and sealed by the college, personnel ID/Passport along with campus card are required to activate campus card’s library privileges. The Service Counter of Main Library or Dewang Library is where users can activate campus card, and ask questions about borrowing privileges and responsibilities. Library privileges are not transferable. Only the individual named on the library card can use the card. For a downloadable borrowing application form, please visit
http://library.xmu.edu.cn/portal-en/secondpage.asp?pid=5&sid=4772
.

All material is subject to recall by another user. Once recalled, item due dates will be shortened to 22 days from the borrowing date, and item that has been kept more than 15 days should be returned within one week.
Return
Return materials to any library circulation desk during open hours, or to the outdoor book drops when libraries are closed. Materials damaged or incomplete should be brought immediately to the owning library circulation desk to discuss repair or replacement options that may be available.
Fines and Fees
For each overdue material, users will be charged RMB 0.2 per day. Borrowing privileges will be blocked until overdue items are returned and fines are paid. Paid overdue fines or replacement fees couldn’t be refunded. Overdue notices are a courtesy, sent to the email address provided in users’ library. Failure to receive a notice does not cancel obligations to pay fines or fees.
Study Space
Xiamen University Libraries offer the opportunity to make use of study seats at the majority of service locations. There are differences across the individual locations as to whether study seats should be reserved and booked in advance, or whether they are free to use on an ad hoc basis. Detailed seat management rules and step-by-step instructions could be found at
http://library.xmu.edu.cn/portal-en/seatmanage.asp
. Xiamen University Libraries also offer online booking service for group study rooms on the 2nd to 4th floor of Main Library through
http://rooms.xmulib.org/en
, and group study rooms on the 5th floor of Dewang Library through
http://172.19.254.242/studyroom/EN/Default.aspx
.
Print, Copy and Scan
Xiamen University Libraries offer a campus-wide, cloud-based printing service, which allows users to send print requests to print-copy-scan machines located in the libraries. In order to print from personal device, download and install the correct print drivers. Machine locations and detailed instructions could be found at
http://210.34.4.89/
. English version could be found by switching language icon on the up right side. Detailed instructions are also available in self-service printing, copying, and scanning area.
Wireless Internet Access (Wi-Fi)
All library locations offer free wireless access (Wi-Fi) in public areas at all times the libraries are open. Options for Wi-Fi access in the library include XMUNET+ and Eduroam. Use personal device''''s network utilities, and look for the network you would like to use. “XMUNET+” requires users to log in Student/Faculty Identification Number and password, which could be setup on the website of
http://p.xmu.edu.cn
. The advantage of using Eduroam over the other networks is that it can be used at other universities that are part of the Eduroam network.
Off Campus Access
Xiamen University students, faculty and staff may access Xiamen University Only materials via connecting from off campus through VPN (Virtual Private Network) Services. Step-by-step instructions and examples could be found at
http://library.xmu.edu.cn/portal-en/proxy.asp
. Before accessing licensed article databases, eBooks and eJournals off campus, make sure to read Conditions of Use and Licensing Restrictions for Electronic Resources. It is the responsibility of individual users to ensure their use of electronic resources does not breach the terms and conditions specified in the license agreements. Lists of digital library resources could be found on the website of
http://library.xmu.edu.cn/portal-en/database.asp?language=eng
.
Interlibrary Loan Services and Fees
Xiamen University Libraries is networked with libraries around the world to obtain materials that are not available. Interlibrary Borrowing assists Xiamen University students, faculty, and staff to obtain books, articles, and other materials not available in teaching, learning and research. Most libraries charge us for loaning materials and for delivering electronic files. We charge RMB 0.2 per page for photocopy or delivery in electronic formats of articles, proceeding papers, ordinary books and dissertations. For rare books scanning, each page fees range from RMB 2-15. For each printed book delivery, we charge users RMB 15.
Campus Card Services
The campus card integrates various functions, such as personal identification, system login and campus payment. In the event of a lost or card-locked, please visit one of the following service counters to report loss, reissue or unlock the campus card (Tel: 2183508).
Student Affairs Hall, 1st floor, Jiageng 3 Building, Siming Campus
General Service Counter, 2nd floor, Main Library, Siming Campus
Information Engineering Library, Haiyun Dorm Area, Siming Campus
Service Counter, 2nd floor, DeWang Library, Xiang’an Campus.

Guidance for Exchange Students
Living Guide in Xiamen University
l
XMU e-card
XMU e-card is issued by Xiamen University, combining the functions of the student ID, library, dining, shopping in campus, etc.
A. Functions
With the XMU e-card, you can live and study in XMU easily without taking too much cash or bank cards. XMU e-card involves information about your student number, name, e-card account, your photo and other personal information, which is useful when dining in the campus cafeteria, entering libraries, borrowing books and shopping in campus.
B. Payment and Recharge
Please link your bank account with your e-card in the bank, then you can easily top up your e-card by transferring money from the bank card to e-card on self-service machines near the cafeteria, maximum 500RMB per time. Cash is not accepted for recharging e-cards. The default password is 123456 and you'd better change it on self-service machines and e-card website as soon as you have the card.
C. Relevant Addresses:
XMU E-card center is located on the 1st floor, Jiageng Building No.3. 24-hour voice call: 2187890
l
Internet
Access
The University WLAN and WIFI is available in overseas students’ dormitory. Please go to China Telecom or China Unicom to purchase the WLAN or WIFI service pack.
For the campus WIFI service, please refer to this website
http://inc.xmu.edu.cn/14/92/c17101a332946/page.htm
for wireless network setup guide.
For Students who need the Internet service can go to the Xiamen University Information & network services Center with your student card.
Address: XMU Internet Center, 1st floor, Jiageng Building No. 3; Tel: 2183508.
Please refer to Xiamen University Information & network services for more information.
http://net.xmu.edu.cn/
Useful Links:
Xiamen University: http://www.xmu.edu.cn
XMU Library: http://library.xmu.edu.cn
School of Management: http://sm.xmu.edu.cn/

XMU Admission Office: http://admissions.xmu.edu.cn/
International Exchange Office: http://ice.xmu.edu.cn/
XMU Teaching Affairs Office: http://jwc.xmu.edu.cn
XMU Postgraduate School: http://gs.xmu.edu.cn/en/
l
Library
Located to the left of the South Gate, covering an area of 22,000 square meters, the XMU library holds over 2,500,000 volumes of books with 500,000 in foreign languages and the number of volumes grows by 100,000 every year. There are systematic book collections in subjects like economics, management, philosophy, history, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology. Besides, XMU library is also for its characteristic materials in Southeast Asian Research and Taiwan Research. More than 40 famous international academic databases are rented or purchased by XMU. Web of Science and other world major academic databases are introduced. Now those databases available in the university LAN contain over 10,000 electronic journals in foreign languages and over 8,000 in language. Meanwhile, the total data amount saved in XMU local servers adds up to 8TB. You can visit the digital library on the Internet or enter the library or borrow the books with your XMU e-card.
l
Dining halls
Besides the dining hall and the coffee house on the first and second floor of Cai Qingjie Building, there are many other dining halls or cafeterias providing good meals and services for students. The following are their names and locations:
A
．
Nanguang Dining Hall near Cai Qingjie Building;
B
．
Furong and Dongyuan Dining Halls near the XMU Supermarket;
C
．
Qinye Dinning Hall near the Da Nan Gate.
All the dining halls and canteens are provided with ultra-red sterilizing cupboard, ensuring high standard food hygiene. Students can buy food with XMU e-cards.
l

Post Office
Xiada Post Office is at Yanwu Road near the campus. At the West Gate (main gate) of Xiamen University, there is an office for incoming and outgoing mail (Xiada Post Box). Letters sent to the students can be claimed at the reception on the second floor of Caiqingjie Building.
Any parcels sent from abroad can be collected by following procedures:
A. Pick up the Parcel-arrival notice at the dormitory reception;
B. Get the parcel form from Xiada Post Box by showing the Parcel-arrival notice and his/her own ID card;
C. Collect the parcel from Xiada Post Office.
l
Banks
Here are Bank of China, China Industrial and Commercial Bank, and China Construction Bank on XMU campus which offer services like currency saving deposit, time deposit, bank transfer, foreign currency transaction, etc.
l
Gymnasium and Stadium
There is a 400-meter standard track and field ground to the opposite side of Qunxian Building near the West Gate of the university. In front of the track and field ground, there are ten basketball courts and several horizontal and parallel bars. To the south of the track and field ground, there are tennis courts and volleyball courts. In front of Jiannan Great Hall, students will find the Shangxian (First Quarter of the Moon) Football Field containing two small football pitches where football lovers can demonstrate their ball skills. Besides that, eight new basketball courts have been set up between the Lingyun dormitory complex and Furong 12 dormitory building. Table-tennis rooms are located at Jianwen Building and Cai Qingjie Buildings. There is a swimming pool with standard tracks as well other facilities in the Qing Ming Swimming Gymnasium. In order to swim there, students need a health certificate issued by XMU Hospital and pay by XMU e-card.

Live Off Campus:
Rent an apartment with other exchange students are very popular. You could easily find many modern, high value for price apartments near the campus. You could share the living room, kitchen and bathroom with your roommates, the furniture and household appliance are provided by the landlord.

Live in Campus
If you are interested in living in student dorms located in the campus, please contact the school coordinator first to register the room or bring your admission acceptance letter to the reception of Cai Qingjie Building. Most of time, the dorms in the campus will be in high demand and reserved for full scholarship students.
Nanguang 4, Nanguang 5 Building and Cai Qingjie Building, located in the center of the main campus are dormitories specially for scholarship students, exchange students, and degreed students. With modern facilities such as air condition, television, telephone, internet access (optional), etc., the buildings provide comfortable accommodation, dining hall, coffee bar, store for overseas students

Welcome International Students 2026
Dear New Students：
Welcome to Tianjin University! In order to better embark on your new life ahead, please read the following notices regarding new-student registration.
Airport Pickup
Tianjin University has prepared free airport pick-up service for all new international students at the
Tianjin Binhai International Airport. For
individual who arrives at other airports, please arrange own transportation to the university for check-in and registration.
Arrangements for Airport Pick-up
Date:
31st Aug. to 2nd Sep.
Time:
9:00-21:00
Location:
Tianjin Binhai International Airport
After collecting check-in baggage, look for a volunteer carrying a sign board with "Tianjin University" written on it at the arrival hall, show your admission letter to the volunteer, after confirmation, you will be taken to the bus.
On-site Check-in
Date and Time
Foundation Program：
31st Aug. to 1st Sep.
Degree Program，General Scholar：
1st Sep. to 3rd Sep.
Location
The welcome stations of the university will be open from 29th Aug. to 4th Sep. Please confirm with your teacher from International Students' Affairs Office about the campus you will be study at and check-in at the specified welcome station for each campus:
Weijin Road Campus Welcome Station
Address：Block A&B, Liuyuan, Tianjin University, Weijin Road No.92, nankai District, Tianjin City
Peiyangyuan Campus Welcome Station
Address: Kela Apratment Block No.2, Tianjin University, Yaguan Road No.135, Jinnan District, Tianjin City
Procedures of Check-in
Step 1: Collect your Welcome Pack, which includes the New Student Guide, International Student Handbook, Campus ID Card, orientation schedule, campus map folder, registration procedure form and registration reminders.
Step 2: Verify your insurance payment receipt.
Step 3: Apply for a mobile SIM card.
Step 4: Open a bank account.
Step 5: Apply for on-campus accommodation or inquire about off-campus housing resources.
Step 6: Complete the 24-hour accommodation registration (record card for inspection).
Step 7: Make an appointment for physical examination for the day after check-in (payment is needed, You may go to the physical examination center via the bus the following day).
Registration
Time for Registration
The arrangement for registration for new international students of Weijin Road Campus:
Date: 2nd Sep. to 3rd Sep.
Time: 8:30 - 12:00, 13:00 - 16:30
Venue: Hall,Liuyuan, Weijin Road Campus, Tianjin University
The arrangement for registration for new international students of
Peiyangyuan Campus
:
Date: 4th Sep.
Time: 8:30 - 12:00, 13:00 - 16:30
Venue: Second Floor ofBlock A, Liuyuan, Peiyang Park Campus, Tianjin University
Documents Needed
Please get the documents prepared before check-in:
Registration Card (Obtain from the welcome station);
Original and photocopy of valid Passport and Visa (X1 or X2);
Electronic Admission Letter;
Electronic “Visa Application Form for Study in China” (Form JW201 or Form JW202);
Original and photocopy of highest degree certificate (Note: For new doctoral students, both bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates must be verified. Graduates from Chinese universities shall present your graduation certificate and degree certificate for verification. For new undergraduate students, the original high school graduation certificate shall be verified. Certificates issued in languages other than Chinese or English must be accompanied by notarized Chinese and English translation.);
10 passport size photos;
Original copy of “Foreigners Physical Examination Report” and blood test report (for students who plan to study in China for a period of more than 6 months);
Except for new students awarded CSC, CIS and MOF scholarships,  new students with other types of scholarships or self-funded new students shall complete online payment of registration fee, tuition fees, medical insurance fee and other required fees before arriving in China, and keep the payment receipts ready for registration.
Procedures of Registration
Step 1:
Pre-document Verification
Step 2:
Fee Payment
Step 3:
System Photo Capture
Step 4:
Personal Information Verification
Step 5:
Accommodation Information Registration
Step 6:
Academic Affairs Processing
Step 7:
China Entry-related Affairs Processing
Step 8:
Student Affairs Information Handover
Notes for Registration
Except for new students receiving CSC, CIS or MOF scholarships, those with other types of scholarships or self-funded students must submit the tuition payment certificate at registration. Failure to settle tuition will prevent completion of the registration process.
If you are unable to attend the centralized check-in and registration on
2nd Sep. to 4th Sep.
for personal reasons, you must complete the procedures in person at Office 401, International Education School Building, Weijin Road Campus, Tianjin University.
Students who cannot register on time must send an explanatory email to the Student Affairs Office of the International Education School of Tianjin University with a copy to the Admissions Office two weeks in advance. Failure to register on time without valid justification for more than two weeks will be regarded as a waiver of admission.

Transportation
Adana, due to its location, is a city with easy access by road, railway
*
, and air. It offers direct bus services from almost all cities in Türkiye, as well as direct or connecting transportation options via trains and flights from many central points. The Mithat ÖZSAN Amphitheatre, where the congress will be held, is located in the Balcalı Campus, approximately 8 km away from the city centre.
*
Please check the railway transportation availability for your convenience as speed-train construction is in progress
.
Bus Transportation:
By bus, you can reach the
Adana Intercity Bus Terminal
, which is 5 kilometres away from the city centre, and from there, you can easily reach the city centre. Within the terminal, there are
shuttles
operated by bus companies,
taxis
, or you can take
minibuses (dolmuş)
or
municipal buses
from the
main road
outside the terminal to reach the city centre. From
İnönü Parkı
or
Atilla ALTIKAT
area, you can easily reach the
Mithat ÖZSAN Amphitheatre
by taking minibuses numbered
4
or
4/B
, or
orange-coloured Balcalı buses
.
Air Transportation:
Transportation from
Çukurova International Airport (COV)
, which serves Adana and the surrounding region, is available through various alternatives. The airport is located approximately
35 km
from Adana city centre and about
45 km
from Çukurova University campus.
From the airport, you can reach the city centre or the university by
taxi
or
airport shuttle services
operating to Adana. Public transportation options also connect the airport to central points in the city.
Once in the city centre, the university campus can be reached by
municipal buses
,
minibuses (dolmuş)
, or other local transportation services. Minibuses numbered
4
and
4/B
departing from
İnönü Parkı
or the
Atilla Altıkat
area, as well as the orange-coloured
Balcalı buses
, provide access to the campus. After entering the campus,
campus transportation vehicles
can be used to reach the
Mithat Özsan Amphitheatre
.
Train Transportation:
Adana Train Station
, located approximately 1.5 km away from the city centre and in a very central location, offers various transportation options to reach the campus. From the station, you can reach the campus by taxi, or you can take
municipal buses
coming to Balcalı Campus from
Atatürk Caddesi
, which is just a few minutes' walk away, or
orange-coloured Balcalı buses
from
Gazipaşa Bulvarı
.
NOTE:
Those opting for municipal buses for transportation can make contactless payments with a credit card or obtain a single-use card from the kiosks near the stops.

How to apply for NENU email for individuals
Step 1:
Find the E-hall service from the website https://www.nenu.edu.cn/index.htm. If you are outside of the campus, please log in to WebVPN first with your student ID number and password. For the first time of login, the password is 10 digitals which are “Nenu+last six number of your passport”, e.g.: Nenu123456. If you have trouble, please go to Room 315 of Vision Building for help. Hotline: 8509-9005.
Step 2:
Log in with your student ID number and password. For the first time of login, the password is 10 digitals which are “Nenu+last six number of your passport”, e.g.: Nenu123456. If you have trouble, please go to Room 315 of Vision Building for help. Hotline: 8509-9005.
Step 3:
If you are not able to choose the language, please input “邮箱”（email）to find the service of “个人邮箱申请”（NENU email application for individuals）. Or go to the G section to find the service of “个人邮箱申请”（NENU email application for individuals）.
Step 4:
Starting the application by clicking the orange button “开始办理”(start application).
Step 5:
Confirm your Chinese Name, Student ID, and School information, input your cellphone number, and choose your email address, if you want to add three numbers to your email address you could choose yes and input three numbers between 100 to 999. After you are done, click the green button on the right to submit your application.
Step 6:
End of application. Login to E-hall to check your email address and change the password.
Note：
If you forget your password or your account is locked, please visit Room 315 of Vision Building or send an email to xxhb@nenu.edu.cn to reset your password.

K22: Get to Know the DNTU Campus Before Starting University
From lecture halls and the library to practice rooms, the dormitory, and sports facilities, the DNTU campus is equipped with a diverse range of facilities to support students’ learning, practical training, research, and daily life. Before officially starting the new academic year, let’s explore the seven buildings from A to G and get familiar with DNTU’s learning environment.
With a total area of 76,130 m², including 52,613 m² of floor space dedicated to education and research, DNTU features a comprehensive campus with facilities designed for various purposes, including administrative areas, lecture halls, a library, practice rooms, a dormitory, sports facilities, and spaces for student activities.
Within the overall campus, the seven buildings A, B, C, D, E, F, and G each serve different functions, creating a well-rounded environment that supports students throughout their academic and university life.
Building A – Administration and Learning Center
Construction of Building A began on January 1, 2004, and the building was upgraded in July 2024. It covers an area of 4,582 m², with three floors and 48 rooms.
The building houses administrative offices, meeting rooms, lecture halls, and an auditorium with a capacity of 200 seats. Building A serves as one of the central areas for the University’s administrative, academic, and program-related activities.
Building B – Teaching and Learning Space
Construction of Building B began on January 1, 2004. In 2008, the building was upgraded with two additional floors. It covers an area of 3,048 m², with four floors and 40 rooms.
Building B primarily serves theoretical teaching and learning, supporting classes and academic activities throughout students’ studies at DNTU..
Building C – Library and Knowledge Hub
Construction of Building C began on January 1, 2004, with upgrades carried out in 2011 and February 2020. The building covers an area of 3,123 m² and consists of two floors.
This is home to the DNTU Library, serving students’ needs for reading, accessing resources, research, and self-study. With a focus on developing learning spaces and digital resources, the library is an important part of the University’s academic and research environment.
Building D – DNTU Dormitory
Construction of Building D began on August 20, 2007. The building covers an area of 5,181 m², with six floors and 92 rooms.
Building D serves as the student dormitory and also includes facilities supporting students’ daily life and learning, such as a canteen, classrooms, and multipurpose lecture rooms. It provides a convenient living and learning environment for students during their time at DNTU.
Building E – Practice and Physical Activity Space
Construction of Building E began on June 20, 2016. The building covers an area of 4,690.7 m² and consists of three floors. In April 2024, the area was further upgraded with facilities including a parking area, football field, and a two-story automotive practice workshop.
Building E combines spaces for professional practice and physical activities, expanding the range of facilities available for students’ learning and hands-on experiences.
Building F – Technology Center
Construction of Building F began on May 1, 2012, and the building was upgraded in July 2023. It covers an area of 5,200 m², with five floors and 45 rooms.
This is one of the main areas at DNTU housing classrooms, practice rooms, and specialized training facilities. Building F supports various fields of study with a diverse range of practice spaces, including 3D Printing, Virtual Reality (VR), the SMC Automation Lab, Information Technology, Accounting, Medicine, Food Technology, Nursing, Food Sensory Evaluation,...
Investing in specialized practice facilities gives students greater opportunities to apply their knowledge, develop practical skills, and gain hands-on experience with equipment and learning environments closely connected to their future careers.
Building G – Complex Center
Construction of Building G began on April 28, 2014. The building was upgraded in March 2023, including improvements to its facade and the classroom spaces of the Faculty of Foreign Languages. It covers an area of 5,576 m², with six floors and 45 rooms.
Building G serves multiple purposes, featuring classrooms, administrative areas, spaces for the Faculty of Foreign Languages, and an auditorium. It also provides facilities for academic activities, seminars, and student programs.
Learning Goes Beyond the Classroom
In addition to Buildings A–G, the DNTU campus features a wide range of facilities supporting student life and activities, including an eight-lane saltwater swimming pool, two football fields, six pickleball courts, as well as volleyball and basketball areas, a gym, and other spaces for student activities.
This diverse campus environment not only meets students’ needs for learning and practical training but also provides opportunities to stay active, participate in extracurricular activities, and enjoy a well-rounded university experience within the same campus.
Located in Dong Nai City, a region with dynamic industrial development, DNTU is well positioned to build an educational environment closely connected with real-world practice and the workforce needs of businesses. This provides a foundation for students to gradually connect classroom knowledge with the practical requirements of their future careers.
A – B – C – D – E – F – G: Get to Know the Campus Before Your First Day
Each building at DNTU has its own function, supporting learning, practical training, research, daily life, and student activities. Together, Buildings A–G form a multifunctional campus where students can learn, develop their skills, stay active, and create experiences throughout their university journey.
For K22, getting familiar with the campus from the very beginning will make the transition into university life and the new academic year more convenient. Over time, the buildings you once had to find your way around will become familiar places associated with classes, practice sessions, activities with friends, and memorable moments at DNTU.
K22, are you ready to explore the DNTU campus from A to G?

HCMUTE Leadership Congratulates Medical Staff on Vietnamese Doctors' Day (February 27th)
Tác giả
:
On the occasion of the 70th anniversary of Vietnamese Doctors' Day (February 27, 1955 – February 27, 2025), the Party Committee, University Council, and the Board of Rectors of Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology and Education (HCMUTE) visited and extended congratulations to the medical staff, officers, and employees working at the university's Medical Station on the morning of February 26, 2025.
HCMUTE leaders visit and congratulate the Health Care Center
During the meeting, Assoc. Prof. Dr. Le Hieu Giang, Deputy Secretary of the Party Committee and President of HCMUTE, expressed his gratitude and appreciation for the contributions of the Medical Station in providing healthcare services to faculty members, staff, and students. With dedication, responsibility, and continuous commitment, the medical team has played a crucial role in ensuring a safe and healthy learning and working environment. The university hopes that the medical staff will continue to uphold their professionalism, maintain their passion for the profession, and continuously enhance their expertise to remain a reliable support for the HCMUTE community.
Following the visit to the Medical Station, Assoc.Prof.Dr.Le Hieu Giang and the university delegation also visited and congratulated the doctors at Thu Duc Regional General Hospital. This visit served as an opportunity for the university to acknowledge and appreciate the contributions of healthcare professionals in caring for the health of faculty, staff, and students.
In addition to the congratulatory activities, Assoc. Prof. Dr. Le Hieu Giang and the hospital's Board of Directors held discussions on potential collaborations in scientific research and the application of technology in medical practice. Both sides agreed to jointly develop technological products such as smart hospital beds, medical support robots, and drones to enhance healthcare services and optimize medical operations in the future.
HCMUTE leaders visit and congratulate doctors at Thu Duc Regional General Hospital
HCMUTE's Medical Station not only provides primary healthcare services but also plays a vital role in disease prevention, first aid, and medical consultation. With a dedicated staff and well-equipped facilities, the Medical Station is always ready to support faculty, staff, and students in any health-related situations.

Your exchange programme at Ostfalia
Ostfalia maintains
partnerships
(external link, opens in a new window)
with a large number of universities and educational institutions around the world.
Some serve the purpose of joint research, others the exchange of teaching staff. However, the majority of these partnerships are aimed at student exchanges for one or two semesters. There are also co-operation agreements with partner universities that allow students from both institutions to obtain a double degree.
Plan your stay at Ostfalia
If you are a student at one of our partner universities and would like to spend part of your studies at Ostfalia, all you need is to be nominated for the exchange by your home university.
The
deadlines
for this are
15 May for the following winter semester
(start in September) and
15 November for the following summer semester
(start in March).
After your nomination, we will contact you directly and explain the application process and the necessary documents and guide you through the steps you need to take.
Facts for our partner universities can be found here [link].

Special English-language programmes for exchange students
Our faculties always try to offer English-language courses to exchange students from their partner universities. These are not complete study programmes in English, but individual courses that are offered in English in a short programme depending on the semester.

All other faculties offer supervision of project work in English for their exchange students on request.
Exchange students also have the option of replacing a final examination with a term paper in English by individual arrangement.
Your visa for Germany
International students require a visa as authorisation to enter Germany. It is usually valid for 3 months. After the visa expires, you can apply for a residence permit (residence permit in accordance with § 16b of the Residence Act - AufenthG) from the relevant immigration authority at your place of residence in Germany. The purpose of residence for studying also includes preparatory study measures (preparatory language courses, attendance at a preparatory college or a comparable institution), as well as doctoral studies (PhD).
You can also apply for a visa to look for a training place or to apply for a degree programme. Information on the requirements can be obtained from the German embassy in your country of origin.
Under no circumstances should you enter Germany with a Schengen visa, as this cannot be converted into a national visa/student visa or extended! After the Schengen visa expires, you must leave Germany!
Citizens of certain countries can initially enter Germany without a visa for short stays (less than 3 months) as long as no gainful employment is intended.
Australia, Israel, Japan, Canada, South Korea, New Zealand and USA
Andorra, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras, Monaco and San Marino
Citizens of EU and EEA countries (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) and Switzerland do not require a residence permit (visa or residence authorisation) to study in Germany.
Current entry requirements and application forms can be found on the homepage of the
Federal Foreign Office
(external link, opens in a new window)
.
Financial requirements
According to German law, non-EU citizens must provide proof of financial resources in the amount of the currently applicable
BAföG maximum rate
(external link, opens in a new window)
for the number of months they plan to spend in Germany.
Please enquire at the German embassy in your home country about the form in which you can provide this proof. The proof must also be presented during your studies each time your residence permit is extended.
Living in Germany
Ostfalia University does not maintain any accommodation itself and is therefore unable to allocate rooms to international students.
However, there are student halls of residence at the Ostfalia campuses in Wolfenbüttel, Wolfsburg and Suderburg, which are managed by the Studierendenwerk Ostniedersachsen.
Information on the respective halls of residence, their facilities and costs can be found on the website of the
Studierendenwerk Ostniedersachsen
(external link, opens in a new window)
. First select your place of study (Wolfenbüttel, Wolfsburg or Suderburg).
You can apply for a room in a hall of residence using the
application form
(external link, opens in a new window)
.
Please note:
1) It is only possible to edit the application form after you have confirmed that you have taken note of the instructions (tick the box and click on "Send").
2) You can enter a maximum monthly rent in the application. However, if you choose an unrealistically low amount here, you will not be offered a room.
3) You can choose different room options in the application. From single apartment to shared flat. Do not choose just one option, otherwise you will not receive an offer if this option is not available.
4) If your application matches one of the available rooms, StwON will send you a room offer. You then only have 2 days to accept it and return the signed documents. After that, the offer expires for you. So check your emails regularly after sending your application.
Your costs
The cost of living is the monthly cost of meeting basic needs such as housing, food and living. Even with a frugal lifestyle, there are items that are equally important for everyone. In certain areas, of course, there is a kind of "special rate" for students - for example, the German Studierendenwerke are very active when it comes to housing and food. A room in a student hall of residence and lunch in the canteen are a good tip for anyone who needs to save money.
Here are the monthly costs for your studies in Germany:
420 EUR: Rent
(with utilities)
There are various rooms of different sizes and numbers of flatmates in the student residences of the Studierendenwerk Ostniedersachsen. Some cheaper, some more expensive. Of course, you can also look for a room in a shared flat independently.
73.84 EUR: Semester fee 443€/6
(this already includes the
Germany semester ticket
)
120 EUR: Health insurance
198 EUR: Catering
Students spend 198 euros a month on food. That's about 46 euros a week and 6-7 euros a day.
10 EUR: Learning materials
(specialised literature and stationery)
Despite digitalisation, you still need books, paper and pens. However, the amount of these expenses varies from subject to subject.
31 EUR: Telephone, internet, radio and television licence fees
Even if the computer room is available at the university, it is almost impossible to save on these costs. Telephone, internet and radio and television licence fees currently amount to just under EUR 19 per month.
46 EUR: Clothing
A new pair of jeans, T-shirts and underwear. German students spend around 46 euros a month on clothing.
65 EUR: Leisure/culture/sport
The
sports programme offered by Ostfalia University Sports
is a great way to save money.
You will therefore need at least €983.00 per month for your studies
This does not include extras such as holidays, electrical appliances and consumables.
Your to dos
Before your journey
If you are studying at one of Ostfalia's partner universities, we would be delighted to welcome you to Ostfalia for one or two semesters as a temporarily enrolled exchange student.
But first, please contact the International Office at your home university to find out what the internal procedure is for nominating for an exchange place.
Application
Your home university must first nominate you for your stay at Ostfalia.
Our International Student Office will then contact you directly and guide you through the application process and enrolment at Ostfalia.
Documents you will need for this
:
1) a scan of your passport or ID
2) an overview of your academic achievements to date at your home university (transcript)
3) a short curriculum vitae in tabular form
4) a scan of your European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) - if you are European. If you do not have an EHIC, you must obtain membership of a German health insurance scheme before enrolling at Ostfalia.
5) Your Learning Agreement (either as a digital Online Learning Agreement - OLA or as a pdf) if you are coming to us as an ERASMUS+ exchange student.
VISUM
If you are a European citizen, you do not need to apply for a visa for the Federal Republic of Germany. However, if you are a citizen of another country, you must apply for a visa. Don't worry, our International Student Office will tell you exactly how to proceed. However, please inform yourself in advance at the German Embassy about the necessary documents and the deadlines for the application.
Rooms
Ostfalia does not have its own halls of residence at its 4 campuses where you can reserve a room. However, there are the halls of residence of the Studierendenwerk Ostniedersachsen
StwON
(external link, opens in a new window)
. As soon as you have been nominated and our International Student Office contacts you, you will also receive detailed information on how to apply for a room at StwON. We will provide you with advice and support when you apply for a room in a hall of residence.
After your arrival
After your arrival
The International Student Office at Ostfalia is also there to help you as soon as you arrive.
During a welcome phase before the start of each semester's courses, we will give you a detailed introduction to the Ostfalia infrastructure. We will also advise and support you with all official registrations and show you the important facilities on your campus.
Arrival and access to your dormitory room
It is important that you let Studierendenwerk Ostniedersachsen know the details of your journey early enough. Only if the StwON staff know exactly when you will be arriving can they leave your room key in a key-safe if necessary. This way, you will have access to your rented room even if there is no member of staff in the hall of residence.
Receiving your access data for the Ostfalia infrastructure and your Deutschland-Semesterticket
You will receive your access data at the Service Desk of our computer centre. We will be happy to assist you. Please note that you will need to identify yourself when you collect your login details, so please take your passport or ID with you.
Registration at the residents' registration office in your place of residence
Students who are staying in Germany for longer than 3 months must register at the relevant residents' registration office. The International Student Office at Ostfalia will help you with this.
Applying for a residence permit
Often the visa is not valid for the entire period of your stay. It is therefore necessary to apply for a subsequent title (residence permit). It is difficult to get an appointment at the responsible local immigration office; there are long waiting times. The International Student Office at Ostfalia will be happy to help you here too.
Initial meeting with your supervising professor - planning your lectures
The International Student Office at Ostfalia will arrange an appointment with your supervising professor. You can then discuss your choice of course or project content and your timetable with him/her.
You can also contact us at any time during your stay at Ostfalia.
Your return
Your return
At the end of their stay, most of our exchange students are amazed at how quickly the time has passed.
The examination phase at the end of the semester demands all your attention once again.
Before you leave, please contact the International Student Office and let us know exactly when you will be travelling back home.
De-registration
Whether you have to actively apply for de-registration at a certain point in time depends on whether you want to de-register with an authority or your health insurance company on the exact day, e.g. to save costs.
In general, if you are enrolled for a limited period of time, your student status will end with the current semester anyway. However, if you need an official document to terminate your enrolment at Ostfalia before the end of the semester (before 28 February and 31 August), you can actively apply for de-registration.
You can find the respective de-registration application [LINK] for your campus on the pages of the Enrolment Office. The International Student Office will be happy to help you if you have any questions.
Deregistration
(town hall, health insurance)
If you are registered at the town hall with your place of residence in Germany, you must of course deregister before travelling home.
The term of health insurance officially covers the entire semester. Of course, you do not want to pay for insurance in Germany once you are back in your home country. In this case, it is therefore necessary to apply for de-registration for the day of your departure and then send the corresponding certificate to the health insurance company to stop the payments.
Proof of residence for your home university
Some of our partner universities require their students to provide official proof of the duration of their stay at Ostfalia. Simply bring the required document to the International Student Office and we will be happy to confirm your period of stay.
Proof of achievement - Transcript of Records
In order to prove your achievements at Ostfalia to your home university, we will provide you with your transcript of records and, if required, a transcript of records.

图书馆
2023.10.10
浏览量:
重庆大学图书馆是中国西部地区最大的图书馆之一，创办于 1930 年，历史悠久，馆藏丰富，管理与服务并重。图书馆以“文献支撑、 文化育人”为办馆宗旨，按照“资源、管理、服务”三位一体协调发 展的建设思路，坚持“读者至上”的服务理念，遵循“智慧与服务” 的馆训，努力将重庆大学图书馆建设成为国内一流、师生满意的创新 型学术图书馆。
重庆大学图书馆按校区和学科布局设立 3 个分馆，包括 A 校区理工图书馆（含声音图书馆），B 校区建筑图书馆，虎溪校区虎溪图书馆（含 4 个舍区书屋、理学分馆、方志图书馆、科幻图书馆），还与学院合作建设有博雅分馆、新闻分馆。馆舍总面积达 59362 平方米，阅览座位 5481 个。图书馆专业馆员 99 名，设综合办公室、学科服务办公室、资源建设部、网络服务部、情报服务部、特藏部、文化育人中心、理工图书馆、建筑图 书馆、虎溪图书馆共 10 个部门，为读者提供全方位的文献服务。馆藏资源丰富，实体馆藏达 517.37 万册，数字馆藏 1424.83 万册 / 件。图书馆有线网络万兆骨干，千兆到桌面，全馆实现无线网覆盖。图书馆拥 有 21 台物理服务器和 381TB 的存储空间，为“双一流”建设、教学科研与拔尖创新人才培养提供了强有力的文献资源保障。
重庆大学图书馆致力于推动学校及社会创新发展提供信息研究及 分析服务，设有教育部首批科技查新站，2018 年获批首批高校国家知识产权信息服务中心，2020 年获批世界知识产权组织在华设立的技术与创新支持中心（TISC）。图书馆积极参与国家、省市级文献资源保 障体系建设，是教育部文献保障体系 CALIS 省级服务中心、重庆市大学联盟资源平台共建单位、重庆市高校图工委常设秘书处所在单位。
重庆大学图书馆馆庆日为每年 10 月 12 日。虚拟形象为书妹儿。吉祥物为学霸雁。
A校区理工图书馆（总馆）地址：重庆市沙坪坝区沙正街 174 号， 邮编：400044。

text_pages:
Deutschlandsemester-Ticket – AStA Homepage
Deutschlandsemester-Ticket
im Solidarmodell
Auf dieser Seite erhältst du alle wichtigen Informationen rund um das  Deutschlandsemesterticket:
Das Studierendenparlament hat sich, auf Basis unserer durchgeführten Umfrage zur Einführung des Deutschlandsemesterter-Tickets, seit dem Wintersemester 2024/25 für das Deutschlandticket im Solidarmodell als Semesterticket entschieden.
60% des regulären Deutschlandtickets
Das Deutschlandsemesterticket bleibt, wie unser aktuelles Semesterticket, ein Solidarticket und wird mit der Überweisung des Semesterbeitrags automatisch erworben.
Digital statt Ostfalia Karte
Ab dem 01.09.2024 steht dir das Deutschlandsemester-Ticket nur noch digital zur Verfügung und steht nicht mehr mit auf der Ostfalia Karte. Bedeutet, nach Validierung der Ostfalia Karte ist kein Semesterticket für das Semester mehr auf der Karte aufgedruckt. Du musst dich dann auf einer
bestimmten Website
(https://asta.ostfalia.de/index.php/link-und-datenschutz-zum-dsemti/) mit deinen Hochschul-Login-Daten einloggen, dort wird dir dann sofort das Ticket angezeigt und du kannst es in dem Wallet deines eigenen Handys speichern.
Du hast noch Fragen zum Ticket? Dann melde dich bei unserem AStA Semesterticketreferenten:
asta-semesterticket@ostfalia.de
!
Was kann ich mit dem Deutschlandsemester-Ticket alles nutzen?
Das Deutschlandsemester-Ticket gilt bundesweit im öffentlichen Personennahverkehr (ÖPNV). Dazu zählen unter anderem U- und S-Bahnen, Straßenbahnen, Trambahnen, Stadt- und Regionalbusse aber auch Regionalzüge (Interregio Express (IRE), Regional Express (RE) , Regionalbahn (RB).
Diese Regionalzüge sind mit dem Deutschlandsemester-Ticket nicht nutzbar!
Einige innerdeutsche Strecken werden von der Fernverkehr AG betrieben, sind aber für Nahverkehrstickets freigegeben. Diese Freigabe gilt momentan nicht unbedingt auch für das Deutschlandsemester-Ticket.
Weiterführende Informationen über Verbindungen der Nahverkehrszüge; S-Bahnen; Busse; Straßen- und U-Bahnen sowie Kinder-, Fahrrad- oder Hundemitnahme, erfahrt ihr hier:
https://www.dein-semesterticket.de
.
